nodes.description: Lifelong allopurinol normalizes serum urate and prevents gout. Whether it slows kidney decline is unproven, since the evidence comes from small uncontrolled studies. Allopurinol should be avoided in pregnancy.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – UMOD.
evidence.snippet: With allopurinol treatment, serum uric acid concentration returns to normal and gout attacks can be entirely prevented.

evidence.reference_title: From juvenile hyperuricaemia to dysfunctional uromodulin: an ongoing metamorphosis.
evidence.snippet: Allopurinol has been suggested as a therapeutic agent, but unfortunately this was based on non-randomised uncontrolled trials with small patient numbers.

nodes.description: Nephrotoxic drugs, volume depletion and dehydration should be avoided; chronic daily NSAID use should be avoided, though short courses may be used for gout before stage 3 CKD. ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy because of fetal harm. A single case report describes a reversible rise in creatinine on fenofibrate.

evidence.reference_title: Fenofibrate increases serum creatinine in a patient with familial nephropathy associated to hyperuricemia.
evidence.snippet: To our knowledge, this is the first patient with FJHN in whom fenofibrate administration was associated to a further impairment in renal function not attributable to rabdomyolysis.

nodes.description: Slowly progressive CKD, usually first noted in the teens, with a bland urinalysis (little or no proteinuria or hematuria).

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – UMOD.
evidence.snippet: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease – UMOD (ADTKD-UMOD) is characterized by normal urinalysis and slowly progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD), usually first noted in the teen years and progressing to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) between the third and seventh decades.

evidence.snippet: They were young men and presented with hyperuricemia and renal dysfunction with no hematuria or proteinuria.

evidence.reference_title: Uromodulin-associated kidney disease.
evidence.snippet: Individuals with UMOD mutations also suffer from hyperuricemia in childhood, and often suffer from gout in their teenage years.

nodes.description: Most pathogenic variants are missense changes or small in-frame deletions in exons 3 and 4, which encode the EGF-like domains and the eight-cysteine (D8C) domain; many replace or create cysteines and disrupt disulfide bonds, so the protein cannot fold. Uromodulin synthesis is markedly reduced in addition to the accumulation of abnormal protein.

evidence.reference_title: A novel uromodulin mutation in autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: a pedigree-based study and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Most are missense mutations and small in-frame deletions within exon 3 and exon 4, where the EGF-like domains and D8C are encoded

nodes.description: Uromodulin supports apical trafficking of the NKCC2 cotransporter in the thick ascending limb. Loss of functional uromodulin causes salt and water wasting and a concentrating defect, and the proximal tubule compensates by reabsorbing more sodium together with urate, which lowers urate excretion. This step is shown in uromodulin knockout mice and in knock-in mice; how much it explains the human hyperuricemia is not measured directly.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – UMOD.
evidence.snippet: Renal replacement therapies such as hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis replace kidney function but are associated with potential complications; kidney transplantation is curative.

nodes.description: Misfolded uromodulin cannot leave the ER of thick ascending limb cells; it binds ER chaperones (BiP, calnexin, PDI) and forms intracytoplasmic aggregates seen on kidney biopsy, with bundled and cystic ER on electron microscopy. Less uromodulin reaches the apical membrane and urine. Some mutant protein escapes, reaches the membrane and forms extracellular aggregates with a dominant-negative effect on co-expressed wild-type protein.

nodes.description: Mice expressing a disease-type cysteine variant develop ER retention of mutant uromodulin, thick ascending limb cell stress, inflammation and fibrosis. A 30% calorie restriction regimen restored autophagy, cleared mutant uromodulin from the ER and prevented or slowed kidney damage, the only mechanism-directed intervention tested in an ADTKD-UMOD model.
Damaged thick ascending limb cells lead to tubular atrophy, interstitial inflammatory infiltrates and fibrosis, without glomerular disease, and to slow loss of kidney function.

nodes.description: Knock-in of a cysteine-to-arginine disease-type variant. Mice develop low urate excretion, fibrosis, immune infiltration and progressive kidney failure with ER retention and ER stress, but no increase in apoptosis.

ENU-derived and knock-in missense lines on the C3H background. Mutant uromodulin fails to mature and accumulates in the ER of thick ascending limb cells, with impaired concentration, low fractional urate excretion, interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. Severity depends on the variant and on zygosity.
